skills.name: Cloudflare
skills.description: Build, deploy and operate real software on Cloudflare — Workers, D1, R2, KV, DNS and domains, Pages, Turnstile and Queues, through the REST API. The capability every Cloudflare-built site or app depends on.

changelog.summary: Four checks for sites that work but are wrong. Nothing may overlap anything else. The typeface has to reach the reader — a stack led by a macOS-only face with no webfont is a different design on every other machine. The interface has to speak the site’s own language, not show English labels and US dates on a Catalan blog. And a title must not say the same thing twice. All four were found on a live site that passed every existing check.

Catches markup that has become words on the page. A favicon data URI carrying a raw <svg> inside its href closed its own <link> tag early, and a stray glyph and quote-bracket rendered on every route of a live site — while the page answered 200, had a title, and had a favicon link, so every structural check passed. The verifier now reads what the browser actually shows.

Adds a check for the palette every generated site lands on. The verifier now reads the colours the page is actually painted in and warns when they are the default cream-and-terracotta (or near-black-and-acid-green) that arrives regardless of subject — the same palette came out of this stack for a carpentry studio and a municipal swimming pool.

Two fixes from watching an agent use it. The verifier crashed outright when one viewport came back without measurements, throwing away every check that had already passed; a failed measurement is now a warning and the rest of the run continues. And the skill now says a failing check is not advice — the agent ran the checks, read the failure, fixed the two easy ones and reported the site as ready anyway.

The link check now asks what a link actually serves. A site shipped with a "See all" link pointing at its own JSON endpoint: it answered 200, so checking the status alone passed it, and a visitor clicking it got raw JSON in the browser. A link in a page is a promise of a page.

The verifier is now part of what "done" means. It shipped in 0.2.0 but was only mentioned in a reference file, so an agent asked to check a site reached for its own browser instead, looked at the page, and missed a missing favicon and a headline sitting outside the column. The skill now says a deploy is not finished until the checks have run and the screenshots have been opened.

Screenshots no longer land inside the skill. The obvious place to run the verifier from is the folder it lives in, which wrote its output into managed files and left the next update unable to complete. They now go to the Orchestra workspace instead.

Fixes a false alarm in the layout check. It compared the boxes of top-level sections, so any page with a full-bleed header or footer was reported as misaligned — and the correctly-built sections were the ones it named. It now compares where the text starts, which is the question a reader actually asks.

The agent can now look at what it deployed. Adds a verifier it runs after every deploy — it renders the site in a real browser and checks the layout holds, the favicon loads, no API token is being served, and no internal link is broken.
First release. Workers, D1, R2, KV, DNS and domains, Pages, Turnstile and Queues through the REST API.

skills.name: Blog on Cloudflare
skills.description: Run a public blog on Cloudflare Workers + D1 — write, preview, schedule and publish posts, manage comments and reactions, report readership. Built on the cloudflare skill.

changelog.summary: Fixes a broken cross-skill path: the verifier was addressed relative to this skill, which only resolves when both skills are installed into the same root. Also requires checking an article page rather than only the homepage, and states that a failing check is not advice.

Removes the starter template. Every blog built from it came out looking the same, so the skill now teaches the judgement — content model, publishing states, comment moderation, feeds and the traps that only appear in production — and leaves the design to the agent.
First release. Write, preview, schedule and publish posts, moderate comments and reactions, and report readership.
